what: src/runtime/market_hours.us_equity_session() approximates ET from a month table (_FULL_DST_MONTHS). March and November always read as standard time (UTC-5), and US exchange holidays are not modelled; its own docstring says so. This was read from the code and reproduced with the rerun on 2026-09-29, not observed live. Effect 1: from the 2nd Sunday of March to Mar 31, and from Nov 1 to the 1st Sunday of November, the real 09:30-10:30 ET hour reads 'extended' and the real 16:00-17:00 ET after-hours hour reads 'rth'. Effect 2: on a US holiday the weekday RTH window reads 'rth'. Consumers: AlpacaClient.close, which chooses between a market order, an extended-hours limit and a deferral; and, from #14241, the Alpaca naked sweep's _breach_state, where 'rth' lets a fresh last-trade breach drive a market exit and outside RTH a stop rests. A wrong read sends those paths down the wrong branch: a market order after hours or on a holiday is refused or deferred, and no exit is attempted in the misread first RTH hour.
